title: Building a game for yourself vs. one to market are different things
author: AuthorMaterial7495
selftext:
This is probably the biggest gap in knowledge I see here.

Almost every post in this sub is asking for feedback on a game someone made who's entire audience consists of themselves.

There's nothing wrong with making a game for yourself and honestly that should be most peoples approach because you really don't have the skills to make something good enough people will pay money for.    
  
 I'm making a super niche GTA style game that takes place on the street I live on in Denver.    
  
I'm not deluding myself into thinking people would want to play this game when there are AAA titles that do every aspect better than I'm going to be able to.   I'm doing it because I thought it would be fun to stage a game on the street I live on and see the actual businesses around me in a game engine.

There is 0 world where people are going to care about this game outside of myself. 

If my goal was to make something that could potentially sell or at least get players I'd be asking myself the following questions

* Which AI games have had any success and have sold?
* What are non traditional games that don't need to be sold on steam?
* What advantages does AI development have over traditional games?
* What games can you make that rely less on obviously AI assets (sound design, character animation, writing)?
* What's a concept that looks fun if you show a 5 second clip of the gameplay?

I can 100% tell you that it's not going to be your indie action RPG game with clunky animation and dialogue written by AI based on some grand idea you have. 

If your goal if more aligned around people actually liking and testing what you are creating, shoot for the next [worms.io](http://worms.io) , some sort of game using real data (think geoguesser/quiz games) or something like SuperHexagon that's a very simple concept not relying on the art/story/etc. and do it extremely well.

comments.author: Aeweisafemalesheep
comments.body:
yeah, so this has people thinking that hobbyism is equal to running a studio. It's like that guy who has the idea for a board game but it's really just art and lore on top of a used template. Like say magic from say 2004 but with a dice roll of d6 mechanic on top and he could go draw the stick figures, print whatever, paste it all onto cardboard and there you go but he's not in the headspace to sell this. And this is the digital one of that.

I love the RTS space. And i'm seeing a funnel so far.

There is that thing i like but it's just new school gfx.

There is that thing i like but bigger with lame GFX.

There is i have experience building something and also I like this aspect of it and that's like the 20 year dev working on this or that system and plugging it into and perhaps improving upon established game systems or whatever.

And there is more from there as we get into people who have expert skill and knowledge and probably not enough cash to do what they want to in order to move art in a direction based upon whatever while having marketing, and forms of upkeep do adult life stuff.

So i get where you're going dude but you're better off having a conversation with a guy who is selling pickaxes and working with dudes who make TNT than yelling at some dude panning the gold in a stream.  

edit - the number of ppl i'm talking to who don't know basics is real bad. And I dont know everything about biz, infrastructer, and marketing, and like niche dom biz either and i feel like a fucking idiot when considering the impact of some legalistic bullshit of deploying software in south korea. Fuck.

replies.author: AuthorMaterial7495
replies.body:
I dunno I guess I could come off as a dick in my original post like Mr.1% commentor said below but really my point was more like people sort of need to pick a lane.   If you aren't someone that is like using AI to assist a real game development process and you want feedback on a game, people to play it etc, the answer isn't to come here and post some poorly thought out game.

It's to limit the scope of what you are trying and not to make the AAA game that you want to play but making something you have the ability to make fun that will get past the 90% of people that just ignore any AI assisted game design.

comments.author: rateddurr
comments.body:
Since this post has devolved into hot takes, here's mine! 

Shouldn't you be your first customer? If you don't like your game, who else will? 

You know if anyone had the answer, game industry would look a lot different and there wouldn't have been endless GTA 6 memes and several multi hundred million dollar fails like Concord.

Ai let's you iterate and try novel ideas. Isn't that what people want? A new experience? Shouldn't people try out their ideas, especially the ones that seem weird at first? Fuxking sorting hay to find a needle? Dude,I would have never dreamed in a million years that's a game people want to play. 


 I think that is where the art is coming in versus all the cookie cutter clones drafted up by people trying to make a hit game by formula. There's no formula. And AI will increasingly make it so that following a formula will land you along with everyone else following the same formula, churning out millions of games published to the void.

Now you right.... This sub supposed to be about ai game dev principals, not us critiquing random ideas. Someone make a different sub for that pls, I'll join. 

But then... Your post not really about ai game dev principals either, so here we are.

End of rant
